textRun.content: Unified Vaccine & Carrier Architecture: Master Reference Document
No capsular serotypes. Biotypes gravis, mitis, intermedius. Toxin gene tox+ vs tox-
No polysaccharide capsule serotype. Antigen is diphtheria toxin protein
tox gene carried by corynephage beta, dtxR regulator
DT, Td, DTaP, Tdap, DTaP-IPV-Hib-HepB (Pediarix, Pentacel, Infanrix hexa)
Diphtheria toxoid IS the antigen. Also source of CRM197 mutant for other vaccines

DT itself used as carrier in Synflorix 19F and MenACWY-DT Menactra. CRM197 is single amino acid mutant of diphtheria toxin used as carrier for Prevnar 13, Prevnar 20, Menveo, Vaxneuvance, Hib-CRM. Links diphtheria disease name to pneumococcal serotype 19F and to meningococcal serogroups A,C,W,Y via carrier
Cross links to Pneumococcal 19F-DT, Meningococcal Menactra DT, Hib-DT, Typhoid Vi-DT conjugates. Same Latin root diphtheria appears as carrier in 4 major conjugate families
No capsule. Antigen is tetanus toxin protein
Tetanus toxoid IS the antigen. Also carrier protein TT

TT used as carrier in Synflorix 18C, MenACWY-TT MenQuadfi / Nimenrix, MenAfriVac PsA-TT Group A, Hib-TT ActHIB / Menitorix MenC-TT, Vi-TT Typbar-TCV typhoid. Links tetanus disease name to pneumococcal 18C and meningococcal serogroups A,C,W,Y and Hib serotype b and typhoid Vi
Cross links tetanus Latin name to pneumococcal 18C-TT, meningococcal ACWY-TT, Hib-TT, typhoid Vi-TT. Tetanus toxoid containing vaccines (DTaP, DTP, Tdap, Td, DT)

Each serotype has distinct repeat unit. Example 19F: (4)-D-ManpNAc-(1-4)-D-Glcp-(1-2)-L-Rhap-(1-OPO3-) with phosphodiester bridge. 19A: same trisaccharide but linkage to Rha 1-3 not 1-2. 6A: Gal-Glc-Rha-(1-3)-Ribitol-P, 6B: Gal-Glc-Rha-(1-4)-Ribitol-P
cps locus between dexB and aliA, genes wzy polymerase, wzx flippase, wciP SNP at 584 determines 6A (Ser) vs 6B (Asn) linkage, rmlABCD for rhamnose in 19F/19A, wchA etc
PCV10 Synflorix GSK, PCV10 Pneumosil SII, PCV7, PCV13, PCV15 Vaxneuvance, PCV20 Prevnar 20, PPSV23 Pneumovax 23
Synflorix: Protein D for 8 serotypes, TT for 18C, DT for 19F. Pneumosil: CRM197 for all 10. Prevnar family: CRM197 for all. PPSV23: no carrier

18C-TT brings tetanus name onto pneumococcal serotype 18C. 19F-DT brings diphtheria name onto pneumococcal serotype 19F. All CRM197 conjugates bring diphtheria mutant name onto every serotype they carry
Links to Diphtheria via 19F-DT and CRM197, to Tetanus via 18C-TT, to NTHi Haemophilus via Protein D carrier, to Meningococcal via same TT/DT/CRM197 carriers
Serogroups A,B,C,W,Y,X based on capsular polysaccharide. Serotypes based on PorB outer membrane protein
Group A: ManNAc-1-phosphate, Group C: sialic acid alpha2-9, Group W: sialic acid-galactose, Group Y: sialic acid-glucose, Group B: sialic acid alpha2-8
cps locus, sia genes for sialic acid synthesis, myn genes
MenACWY-DT Menactra, MenACWY-CRM Menveo, MenACWY-TT MenQuadfi / Nimenrix, MenC-CRM Menjugate, MenC-TT NeisVac-C / Menitorix, MenA-TT MenAfriVac, MenB protein Bexsero, Trumenba
DT for Menactra, CRM197 for Menveo, TT for MenQuadfi/Nimenrix/MenAfriVac/Menitorix, OMV for MenB

Menactra serogroups A,C,W,Y conjugated to diphtheria toxoid links diphtheria Latin name to meningococcal serogroups. MenQuadfi conjugated to tetanus toxoid links tetanus Latin name. Menveo conjugated to CRM197 links diphtheria mutant
Exact same carriers as pneumococcal: DT, TT, CRM197, Protein D, OMPC. So meningococcal serogroup A-TT links to pneumococcal 18C-TT via shared tetanus carrier
Serotypes a,b,c,d,e,f based on capsule. Type b most invasive. Non-typeable NTHi no capsule
Type b: polyribosylribitol phosphate PRP repeat
cap locus, bexABCD export, region II serotype specific
Hib-TT ActHIB / Hiberix, Hib-CRM HbOC, Hib-OMP PedvaxHIB, Hib-TT in Menitorix
Hib-TT links tetanus name to Hib serotype b via TT carrier. Hib-CRM links diphtheria mutant name to Hib b
Shares TT with pneumococcal 18C-TT and meningococcal ACWY-TT. Shares CRM197/DT with pneumococcal 19F and meningococcal ACWY-CRM/DT. Protein D carrier in Synflorix is derived from NTHi
Serovar Typhi, Vi capsular antigen positive, O9, H:d
viaB locus in SPI-7 pathogenicity island, tvi genes
Vi-PS Typhim Vi (no carrier), Vi-TT Typbar-TCV, Vi-CRM investigational
TT for Typbar-TCV, CRM197 for Vi-CRM
Vi-TT links tetanus Latin name to typhoid Vi serotype via TT carrier. Vi-CRM links diphtheria mutant to Vi
Links typhoid disease name to tetanus and diphtheria via carrier, parallel to pneumococcal and meningococcal linkage
Capsular serotypes Ia, Ib, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX based on polysaccharide terminal sialic acid residues
Sialic acid-containing capsular polysaccharides, structurally similar to pneumococcal and meningococcal capsules
cps locus (cpsA through cpsK genes), homologous organization to S. pneumoniae
No licensed human vaccines yet. Investigational GBS6 CRM197 conjugate, GBS-NN protein
CRM197 (in GBS6), TT, or native protein carriers
CRM197 carrier links the diphtheria mutant name directly to GBS serotypes Ia-V via the same carrier platform used for pneumococcal and meningococcal vaccines
Links GBS to Pneumococcal and Meningococcal disease via shared CRM197 and TT carrier platforms; shares sialic acid chemical architecture
Salmonella enterica serovars Enteritidis and Typhimurium
Bacterium - Gram negative rod - facultative anaerobe
Kaufmann-White serotyping scheme based on O, H, and Vi antigens
Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) O-antigen repeating units (O4, O5, O12 for Typhimurium; O1, O9, O12 for Enteritidis)
Investigational glycoconjugate vaccines; standard whole-cell/subunit veterinary vaccines
TT or CRM197 carriers covalently linked to O-antigen polysaccharides, bridging enteric lipopolysaccharides to classical tetanus and diphtheria carrier strategies
Cross-links enteric Gram-negative non-typhoidal salmonellosis to Tetanus and Diphtheria via carrier proteins, mirroring Hib and meningococcal conjugate design
Bacterium - Gram negative rod - encapsulated/O-antigen bearing
Serovar Paratyphi A, O2, O12, H:a antigens, specific O-antigen polysaccharide chains
wba/rfb gene clusters for O-specific polysaccharide synthesis
Investigational O-antigen polysaccharide conjugate vaccines (O-SP-TT, O-SP-CRM197)
TT or CRM197 used as carrier proteins for Paratyphi A O-specific polysaccharides
Links paratyphoid fever to Typhoid fever (Vi conjugates), Tetanus (via TT), and Diphtheria/Pneumococcal families (via CRM197)
Fungus - yeast - encapsulated - classic bridge between fungi and bacteria
Serotypes A,B,C,D based on capsular glucuronoxylomannan GXM
GXM: mannose backbone with xylose and glucuronic acid side chains
CAP genes for capsule synthesis, similar to bacterial cps concept
No licensed human vaccine. Investigational GXM-protein conjugates using TT, DT, CRM197
Experimental cryptococcal serotype A-GXM conjugated to TT or DT directly parallels pneumococcal 18C-TT and 19F-DT (the fungal-bacterial bridge)
Strongest cross link: Cryptococcus serotypes A-D use same capsule chemistry logic as pneumococcal serotypes, same carrier strategy TT/DT/CRM197, same DNA locus concept

Diphtheria toxoid (DT), its non-toxic mutant CRM197, and Tetanus toxoid (TT) convert T-independent polysaccharide antigens into T-dependent neoantigens, stimulating class-switching and long-term immunological memory.

Because multiple vaccine groups (Pneumococcal, Meningococcal, Hib, Typhoid, and GBS) rely on identical carrier footprints, they form an interconnected network where an immune response to one carrier primes cellular machinery across disparate disease families.

Pre-existing high titers of anti-carrier antibodies can lead to rapid clearance or decoy binding of subsequent conjugate doses, suppressing nascent polysaccharide-specific B-cell activation. Manufacturers mitigate this by diversifying carriers (e.g., using Protein D or OMPC).
In pneumococcal serotypes 6A and 6B, a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) at position 584 in the
gene determines a 1-3 vs. 1-4 linkage on the ribitol-phosphate backbone.
) controls GXM production, proving that fungal pathogens utilize the exact same structural logic and conjugate architecture as bacteria.
DT, Td, DTaP, Tdap, Pediarix (DTaP-HepB-IPV), Pentacel (DTaP-IPV/Hib), Infanrix hexa (Hexavalent), and Menitorix (MenC-TT / PRP-TT).
MMR (Measles, Mumps, Rubella), MMRV (ProQuad), and Twinrix (Hepatitis A & B), utilizing live-attenuated strains and viral surface antigens to bypass the toxoid-conjugate network.
Major fungal pathogens deploy complex extracellular polysaccharide matrixes and cell wall glycans that directly parallel bacterial capsular serotypes and carrier platforms. For instance,

utilizes a glucuronoxylomannan (GXM) capsule that functions identically to bacterial capsular polysaccharides by mediating immune evasion and requiring conjugation to proteins like Tetanus Toxoid (TT) or CRM197 to induce T-dependent antibody responses. Similarly,
galactomannan structures reflect bacterial O-antigen and capsular repeat architectures, providing key targets for experimental glycoconjugate vaccine platforms.
Antiphagocytic polysaccharide capsule composed of alpha-1,3-mannan backbone with xylose and glucuronic acid side chains.
Pneumococcal CPS (e.g., Serotype 18C, 19F) and Meningococcal serogroups A/C/W/Y.
Experimental GXM-TT, GXM-DT, and GXM-CRM197 glycoconjugates yielding robust protective IgG responses.
Outer cell wall layer consisting of highly branched phosphomannans covalently linked to beta-1,3/1,6-glucan structural mesh.
Salmonella O-antigens and Hib PRP repeating polysaccharide units.
Beta-glucan and beta-mannan conjugates (e.g., beta-glucan-CRM197, mannan-BSA) in pre-clinical evaluation.
Extracellular matrix and cell wall polysaccharide comprised of galactofuranose-containing chains and galactosaminogalactan (GAG).
Enteric Gram-negative LPS/O-antigen and capsular exopolysaccharides.
Investigational galactomannan and GAG protein-conjugate formulations aimed at invasive aspergillosis protection.
